keyPoints: The team has completed the evaluation of six criteria using a seven-point scale, with most ratings at the higher end.
The prototype meets the criteria for incorporating current fashion trends and being easy to locate.
The lowest rating is for minimising repetitive strain injury, with a four, as the button size and material may not fully prevent strain.
The team is happy to proceed with producing the prototype and marketing it, as current technology and capabilities are sufficient.
The finance team is now being shown the electronic setup, which includes a double-curved chip on print for the electronics.
The team discussed the lack of attention to remote control innovation compared to mobile phones and TV products.
The team noted that people rarely consider the remote control as the main product, focusing instead on the device it controls.
The team observed that while mobile phone modifications are highly desired, similar innovation for remotes is less common.
The team discussed the market research-based nature of the project, highlighting that remote control changes are now more visible.
The team reflected on the idea of designing individual, funky remotes, suggesting people would pay more for custom designs.
The celebration may involve a twenty-five pounds reward or dancing on desks.
